# Family Wall

> A household dashboard for one family. It holds to-dos, the shopping list, notes, recurring
> chores, identity documents with expiry dates, recipes and an air fryer guide. Next.js +
> Postgres on Vercel. A wall tablet in the kitchen renders the same data read-only.

Written for agents: Muse, Grok, Hermes, Claude, ChatGPT, or anything else that lands here.
If you are a person, the app is at `/`.

## Read this before you touch anything

- This is a live household's data, not a sandbox. Everything you see is real.
- **Ask before deleting.** Deletes are permanent; there is no trash, no undo, no history.
- Attribute writes to the person who asked: `who` / `owner` must be a member id, never invented.
- Never create rows called "test", "probe" or similar and leave them behind.
- Do not touch any other workspace, database, or Notion workspace. This site is the family's;
  business data lives somewhere else and is off limits.
- Data is written in Spanish. Interface chrome is English. Match whatever is already there.
- Poll no faster than once a minute; the wall itself polls every 60 seconds.

## Doors

| Who | How |
| --- | --- |
| People | `/` — HTTP Basic, one username per member |
| Wall tablet | `/frame/<token>` — exact token in the path, read-only, no credentials |
| Agents | the same Basic auth as people, **or an agent key** (preferred) |
| Browser agents | `/agent-login?k=<key>` once: sets a 30-day cookie and lets a cloud browser in |

Writes need no session and no cookie: the middleware resolves the Basic user and passes
`x-member` to the route.

```bash
# a person
curl -u "member:password" https://your-domain.example/api/items

# an agent with a key
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" https://your-domain.example/api/items
```

**Agent keys.** If you were given a key (Muse, Hermes, any other agent), send it as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-agent-key: <key>`. Writes are then attributed to the agent
(`created_by: "muse"` / `"muse-jordan"`). **Always set `who` to the person you are acting for** — an item with
`who: null` does not say whose it is, and the family cannot tell whether it was for Alex or Jordan.
Each person has their own agent key (`muse` for Alex, `muse-jordan` for Jordan), so the
history shows who acted and for whom. A browser that cannot
answer the HTTP Basic dialog should open `/agent-login?k=<key>` once — it sets an HttpOnly cookie
for 30 days and redirects to the app.

There is no public sign-up and no API key. If you were not given a member's credentials,
you cannot read or write anything — and guessing is not acceptable.

## Member ids

`alex`, `jordan`, `maya` — and `any` for "whoever gets to it".
These ids are what `who` and `owner` fields expect.

## What lives where

- **items** — tasks (`task`), shopping (`shop`), notes (`note`). `/api/items`
- **chores** — recurring work, one lane per person, resets by period. `/api/chores`
- **documents** — passports, IDs, permits, licences, with issue and expiry dates. `/api/documents`
- **recipes**, **plants**, **air_fryer** — their own tables and endpoints
- **calendar** — *not stored here*. The family Google Calendar is the source of truth, and the
  wall reads it from ICS feeds. Do not try to store events in this database: `POST /api/items`
  with `kind: "event"` is rejected on purpose and returns a hint.

## API

### Items

```http
GET    /api/items[?includeDone=1]   -> { items: [{ id, kind, title, detail, who, done, due_at, created_by, created_at }], count }
POST   /api/items                   -> 201 { item }
PATCH  /api/items/{id}              -> { item }
DELETE /api/items/{id}
```

- `POST` body: `{ kind: "task" | "shop" | "note", title, who?, detail?, due_at? }`
- `PATCH` accepts only `done`, `title`, `detail`.
- `GET` returns open items only unless you pass `includeDone=1`.

```bash
curl -u "member:password" -X POST https://your-domain.example/api/items \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind":"shop","title":"Leche 2%","who":"jordan"}'
```

### Chores

```http
GET    /api/chores                  -> { chores: [...] }
POST   /api/chores                  -> 201 { chore }
PATCH  /api/chores/{id}
DELETE /api/chores/{id}
```

- `POST` body: `{ title, who, routine?, freq }`
- `freq`: `daily` | `weekly` | `biweekly` | `monthly`
- `routine`: `morning` | `after` | `evening` | `any` (the lane on the wall)
- `PATCH` accepts `title`, `who`, `routine`, `freq`, `done`.

**What "done" means.** A chore is done if it was ticked within the current period, so it
comes back on its own: `daily` = today, `weekly` = this calendar week (resets Monday),
`biweekly` = within the last 14 days, `monthly` = this month. Ticking marks today and
records who did it.

### Documents

```http
GET    /api/documents               -> { documents: [...] }
POST   /api/documents               -> { document }
PATCH  /api/documents               -> { document }   (body must include id)
POST   /api/documents/{id}/file     multipart, field name "file" (pdf, jpg, png)
GET    /api/documents/{id}/file     streams the scan; auth required
```

- Fields: `country`, `doc_type`, `number`, `issued_on`, `expires_on` (YYYY-MM-DD), `owner`, `note`.
- Scans never live in `public/`: they are stored privately and served through the
  authenticated route above.
- A document expired or expiring within **120 days** becomes an alert on the wall.
  Keep `expires_on` accurate; that field is what the house relies on.

### The wall writes exactly one thing

The frame token (`?token=`) is otherwise read-only. The single exception is

```http
POST /api/frame/chores/{id}?token=<FRAME_TOKEN>   { "done": true }
```

which ticks or unticks a chore and nothing else — no create, no delete, no documents. Middleware
allows it by path and method, so a copied wall token can annoy the chore list, not the house. Agents
should keep using `PATCH /api/chores/{id}`.

### Deleting is reversible

`DELETE /api/items/{id}` (and chores, moments, documents) does **not** destroy the row: it marks
`deleted_at` and the row leaves every list. It stays in the trash for 30 days.

```http
GET  /api/trash                                   -> { rows, count, days }
POST /api/trash  { "table": "items", "id": 12, "action": "restore" }
POST /api/trash  { "table": "items", "id": 12, "action": "purge" }   -> 403 for agent keys
```

An agent key may **restore** but never **purge** — only a person can empty the trash. If you delete
something by mistake, restore it; do not re-create it, which would leave two of it.

### Backup

```http
GET /api/export
```

Full JSON dump of the six tables. Use it for backups, not to read one list.

## Recipes and plants

`GET` and `POST` on `/api/recipes` and `/api/plants`; `PATCH` on `/api/plants`.
`/api/air-fryer` is `GET`/`POST`. These are read-mostly: if the person asks you to change
one, read the existing row first and match its shape.

## The wall

`GET /api/frame` returns exactly what the kiosk draws: items, people, weather, calendar,
chores and expiry alerts. It is a rendering payload, not an integration surface — do not
write to it.

## If you are unsure

Read first (`GET /api/items`, `GET /api/chores`), then act on the smallest change that
satisfies the request, then read again to confirm it landed. If a request would delete
something, or touches documents and scans, ask the person before doing it.
